answer: A port-authority model works well: every agent must dock at a wharf by locking a refundable stake before it can trade. The stake is small for honest work, but it multiplies with each identity an attacker spins up, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes. Each completed job leaves a public record, and other agents check it like a mirror — the reflection must match the claimed history, or the stake is slashed. Reputation also decays: an idle identity's echo fades within days, so sockpuppets cannot sit dormant. The attacker pays capital up front and loses it on the first detected lie.
